grades.reason: Describes the layered structure and on-disk layout of the xv6 file system. It says nothing about seek time or rotational latency, so it doesn't explain why same-size reads take different times.

grades.quote: Once the appropriate track is spinning under the active head, the disk controller needs to wait for the appropriate sector to come around to the head’s position, a delay known as _rotational latency_ .
grades.reason: Directly explains the cause. Seek time depends on how far apart the tracks are, and rotational latency depends on where the sector sits relative to the head. Locality and sequential versus separate requests also change access time.
Covers extent maps versus block maps and the extra I/O operations that indirect blocks cause. It doesn't address the mechanical causes of latency variation in a rotating disk for equal-sized reads.
About races and mutual exclusion in synchronization. It is unrelated to disk access latency.
